manifest.name: dsh-plugin-upgrader
manifest.description: DSH plugin for DeepSeek Harness: upgrade plugins from the Plugins page, version history, rollback, live pnpm progress
manifest.author: zuwenyin

scripts.check: tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node scripts/build.mjs && node --test && node scripts/verify-pack.mjs && node scripts/verify-build-committed.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh bundle patch: inserts this plugin into the profile's layer stack.
# One row mounts both halves: the host half (registry packument proxy +
# upgrade/rollback job runner) and the browser half (the "版本" tab that the
# Plugins page renders next to Installed and Discover).
- insert:
    - id: plugin-upgrader
      name: dsh-plugin-upgrader

readme.text:
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-upgrader)
[](./LICENSE)
[](https://www.dsh.so/artifact/dsh-plugin-upgrader/)
[](https://www.dsh.so/artifact/dsh-plugin-upgrader/)
[](https://dsh.market/)
[](https://deepseekharnessplugins.com/plugins/zuwenyin/dsh-plugin-upgrader)

> 给 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的「插件」页补上**一键升级**和**版本历史 / 回滚**。

DSH 自带的插件页能装、能卸、能看已安装列表，但缺两件事：一次把全部插件升到最新，以及退回某个旧版本。
这个插件在插件页里加一个「版本」标签，把这两件事补齐。

[English](./README.en.md) · 中文

- **一键升级** —— 一次把全部可升级插件升到最新版，带进度、逐项结果和失败原因。
- **升级不卸载** —— 换版本走 in-place 替换，插件不会被卸下来再装回去（详见下文）。
  拿不到 profile 写入锁、或 in-place 那一步被拒时，会退回「先卸载再装」的老路并写明原因。
- **看得见的进度** —— 升级时直接显示 pnpm 的原始输出（含换源重试、lockfile 校验），
  每步都有已用时计时和不确定态进度条，卡住时可以一键取消。
- **多选升级** —— 勾选任意几个插件，只升级选中的这些。
- **版本历史 / 回滚** —— 展开任意插件即可看到已发布的全部版本（含发布时间与引擎要求），点一下切到那个版本。
  每个版本都会先跟你**当前跑的 DSH** 比对一次：装不了的版本会被标出来，切换按钮也是禁用的
  （宿主的兼容性闸门是在 bundle 已经卸下之后才拒绝的，不能让它走到那一步）。
- **一键跳 GitHub** —— 每行的 `GH` 按钮打开插件仓库主页；点版本号直接进该版本的 GitHub 发布页。
- **镜像落后会标出来** —— 配置的镜像还没同步、但上游已经发布的版本会单独标一行，
  而不是假装已经是最新版。
- **自己选安装源** —— 版本页顶部就能切换 npm 源（官方源 / 大陆镜像 / 自己填的私有源），
  选完立刻按新源重读版本列表，升级也走这个源；选择写进 profile，重启和换浏览器都还在。
- **安装源管理** —— 「注册表」按钮打开一个对话框，里面列出自带源、`pluginManager` 配的源
  和用户自己加的源；自带源不能改也不能删，自己加的可以随时改/删。每一行都能单独
  「测试」能不能连上，当前在用的那个也能一键测。
- **要重启时告诉你怎么重启** —— 升级结果里带 `restart-required` 时，提示条上多出一个
  「重启 DSH」按钮，点开说明为什么这次改动要等，并按你的启动方式给出那一条能完成重启的
  操作：桌面版是「退出应用再打开」，命令行启动的是可复制的原命令。确认重启后它会盯着
  宿主的 pid，换了进程才刷新页面，而不是让你对着一个不确定的页面猜。
- **最新版装不了时，给出能装的那个** —— 宿主的兼容性闸门是在 bundle 已经卸下之后才拒绝的，
  所以最新版在你的 DSH 上跑不了时，页面不会只留一行死掉的「升级」：它会算出「高于已装、
  并且这台宿主真的能装」的最高版本，按钮变成「升级到 1.1.0」，批量升级也走这个目标。
  这个推荐**永远不会高于** `latest`，tag 之后发布的预发布版不会被它提拔。
- **「你现在跑的这个」也会不兼容** —— 上面那句话是从最新

> **要改这个仓库？先读 [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)。** 那里逐条写了「已经实现并且必须继续成立」
> 的行为、对应代码位置和守护它的测试。上面这些功能里，`GH` 链接和 in-place 升级都曾经
> 被无意改掉过一次。

插件页顶部标签栏多出一个「版本」标签，与「已安装」以及市场标签并列
（市场标签在装了 `dshmarket` 的界面里叫「插件市场」，DSH 自带的那个叫「发现」）：

- 顶部统计：需处理数量 / 可升级数量 / 已安装数量 / 每个插件的版本数
  （「需处理」可以点，点了只看有问题的行；和搜索框能叠加）
- 顶部「注册表」按钮打开安装源对话框：
  - 自带源（官方源、大陆镜像）：只能切过去和测试，不能改也不能删
  - `pluginManager` 里配的源：可以「收进列表」变成自己的常用源，或直接用
  - 自己加的源：可以改、可以删，删掉的如果正在用会自动退回「跟随 pnpm 配置」
  - 每行「测试」同时打 `/-/ping` 和根地址，谁先答应用谁，整次探测 5 秒预算
    （串行探测会把大陆镜像报成连不上：`/-/ping` 有时要 15 秒，根地址只要 0.3 秒），
    结果显示在那一行下面
  - 底部「跟随 pnpm 配置」用 pnpm 自己的源（通常是 `~/.npmrc` 里的那个）
- 「一键升级」升全部可升级插件；下面一条选择栏负责「升级选中」
- 「检查更新」强制刷新 registry 缓存（默认缓存 5 分钟）
- 搜索框按包名过滤
- 页脚写明当前读到的 DSH 版本，以及这次列表是从哪个 registry 读出来的
- 「复制诊断信息」把版本、registry、每一行的问题拼成一段 markdown，贴进 issue 就行
- 每个插件一行，展开「历史 (n)」后是该插件的完整版本列表
- `GH` 打开仓库主页（没有仓库的插件不显示该按钮）
- 版本列表里每个版本号本身就是链接，点开直接进 GitHub 的发布页：
  - 该版本打过 tag → `releases/tag/v<version>`（tag 是否真实存在由 GitHub tag 列表确认，
    不是猜的，所以不会点进 404）
  - 该版本没打 tag，或 GitHub 列表读不到（限流 / 离线）→ 退回仓库的发布列表 `releases`，
    不在页面上放一个点进去是 404 的版本号

在「插件」页的市场标签里搜索 `dsh-plugin-upgrader`（自带的是「发现」，
装了 `dshmarket` 的界面里叫「插件市场」），点安装即可。
桌面版请用它自带的插件管理界面安装，命令行改动不了正在运行的桌面 profile。

用 `dsh` 命令行（把 `web` 换成你自己的 profile 名）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-upgrader
```

从源码安装：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zuwenyin/dsh-plugin-upgrader.git
cd dsh-plugin-upgrader
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD"
```

装好后打开「插件」页，顶部会多出「版本」标签。不需要重新构建，也不用重启。

浏览器端读不到 profile 的依赖清单，也无法可靠直连 npm（CORS、私有源、token），
因此所有包操作都放在宿主端：

| 路由 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/plugin-upgrader/overview` | 已安装插件 + 各插件已发布版本（registry packument，5 分钟缓存，20 秒超时，最多 4 个并发） |
| `POST /api/plugin-upgrader/job` | 提交一批升级 / 切换步骤，立即返回 job id |
| `GET /api/plugin-upgrader/job?id=…` | 轮询进度、当前阶段、已用时、逐项结果与实时日志 |
| `POST /api/plugin-upgrader/cancel` | 中断当前步骤（任何一次安装，包括退回老路径后的重试） |
| `GET /api/plugin-upgrader/host` | 本进程的 pid 与启动方式，供「重启 DSH」对话框说明怎么重启 |
所有路由仅限本机回环访问：批量操作会安装软件包，配对设备或跨站页面一律拒绝。

readme.section: 为什么升级不卸载插件
readme.text:
`pluginManager.installBundle` 对已安装的包名会以 `already-installed` 拒绝，
pnpm 根本不会跑。所以换版本的顺序是：

1. **先直接 `install`**；
2. 被拒绝时，把 profile `package.json` 里那条依赖**临时**摘掉（先写 journal），再 install ——
   pnpm 写回新版本，**插件不被卸载**，加载器里的实例不断，启用状态也不用恢复；
3. 只有第 2 步主动放弃（manifest 读不了 / 拿不到写入锁 / install 失败 / 被拒绝）时，
   才退回 remove + install 的老路径，并在日志里说明是哪一种。

readme.section: 为什么升级不卸载插件
readme.text:
第 2 步改动 `package.json` 时会**拿 harness 自己的写入锁**（`package.json.lock`），
与 `plugin-manager` 用同一把锁：拿不到锁就一秒内放弃、**一个字节都不写**，
然后走第 3 步那条永远正确的老路——比在别人的 read-modify-write 中间插一脚、
把条目弄丢要好得多。

旧版本号会回传给界面，用于提示这是降级。

> 实现在 1.2.0 就有了，但 1.2.0–1.4.0 在桌面端**从未真正生效**：
> `profileDirFrom()` 只认 `DSH_PROFILE_DIR` / `DSH_HOME` + `DSH_PROFILE`，而桌面壳启动宿主时
> 不导出这些变量（它直接把 profile 目录当作子进程的 cwd），于是第 2 步第一行就放弃了，
> 每次升级都悄悄走 remove + install。1.4.1 加了 cwd 回退之后才真正走这条路。
> 细节见 [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) 第 2 条「换版本时**不先卸载**」。

readme.section: 升级中断后 profile 还能自己长回来
readme.text:
第 2 步要在「依赖条目已经删掉、新版还没装上」的窗口里改 profile 的 `package.json`。
如果进程正好在这段时间被杀掉，插件就从 manifest 里消失了，等于装不回去。
所以删除之前先写 `package.json.upgrader-journal.json`：下次插件加载时会读它，
manifest 里确实缺这条就补回去，已经装上就只清掉记录，记录和 manifest 对不上就忽略。
恢复失败只是打日志，不会拦住标签页加载。

记录只在**锁内确认条目真的回到盘上**之后才清掉。还原那一步如果拿不到写入锁，
它宁可失败并留下记录，让下次加载再修一次——把记录清了却没能写回去，
才是真的没法自愈。

卸载会丢掉插件原有的启用 / 禁用状态，因此任何**真的卸载过**插件的步骤都会在装完后
按操作前的状态重新 `setBundleEnabled`（`src/host/install.ts:251` `restoreEnabledState`），
禁用中的插件升级后仍然是禁用状态。in-place 那条路不卸载，所以本来就不需要恢复。

readme.section: 为什么升级有时候要好几分钟
readme.text:
不是这个插件慢，是 pnpm 慢。pnpm 11 在 `install` 前会拿锁文件里的每个条目去 registry
重新核对一次（`Verifying lockfile against supply-chain policies`），国内镜像
（`registry.npmmirror.com`）对不少包会 `ETIMEDOUT`，于是走 10 秒 → 1 分钟的重试阶梯。
真正卸载再安装的那种降级路径要跑两条 pnpm 命令，两段各等一次。

旧版本在这里什么都不显示，进度条只在「整步完成」时动一格，所以看起来就是死住了。
现在宿主端订阅了 `plugin-manager/install-log` 和 `plugin-manager/install-state`，
把 pnpm 的原始输出、当前阶段、重试次数实时转进 job 日志，界面同时显示已用时和
不确定态进度条：慢的时候你能看见它在重试，而不是盯着一个不动的 0%。

readme.section: 为什么升级有时候要好几分钟
readme.text:
阶段一共四个：`verifying`（在校验锁文件）→ `installing` → `applying` / `cancelling`。
锁文件校验那一行会连续几分钟不动，单看和「卡死」一样，所以单独给它一个阶段名。

阶段是**按 pnpm 自己的话**判的：manager 是在 pnpm 启动**之前**就上报 `installing` 的，
所以 pnpm 后来的校验行必须还能把阶段改写成 `verifying`，一直到它给出结论
（`✓ Lockfile passes supply-chain policies`）为止。

「还在动」问的是**宿主**，不是 pnpm。pnpm 重试的时候一分钟不打印一行是正常的，
按「日志没变」判停滞会把健康的升级误报成卡住；宿主每 2 秒盖一次心跳，
面板用心跳判定活性，宿主真的不说话了才会说「状态已停止更新」。

顺带修掉的两个坑：

readme.section: 为什么升级有时候要好几分钟
readme.text:
- 心跳改成定时器（2 秒），不再按「完成一步」写。单步超过 15 分钟以前会被误判成
  「job 已放弃」，于是一个健康的任务被作废，还能再并进来一批。
- 退回老路径时那一次重新安装以前用 `requestId: undefined`，导致那一段无法取消；
  现在每次安装都有自己的 id，取消在任何阶段都有效。

profile 的 `package.json` 由 harness 用同目录的 `package.json.lock` 串行化。
manager 自己的预算是 120 秒，而 `atomic-write` 给不写预算的调用方的默认值是 2 秒，
所以偶尔能看到：

```
atomic-write: timed out waiting for the writer lock at …/package.json.lock
```

这句话只报一个文件名和一个 pid，用户无法处理。现在失败信息会先读那把锁，再说清楚是
「另一个操作正在改写，等它结束再试」还是「锁没释放，重启 DSH 会自愈」，
原文放在方括号里保留，方便搜索或贴进 issue。

readme.section: 自己那一行不能自己升级
readme.text:
批量升级的第一步是卸载，而卸载的正是此刻在跑的那段代码。所以「一键升级」永远跳过本插件自己，
自己那一行落后时走插件页自己的安装流程；页面没有提供安装入口时明确说一句，
而不是让人点一个必然失败的按钮。

宿主端一次只允许一个 job。重复提交会拿到 `409 busy`（带正在跑的那个 job id），
界面据此**接管**那一批的进度显示，而不是弹一条看不懂的错误：

- 新开一个插件页标签、或在进度跑着时再点「一键升级」，都会看到正在进行的那一批
- `overview` 里带 `active` 字段，标签页一挂载就能接上正在跑的任务
- job 每 2 秒刷一次心跳时间戳，宿主重启后遗留的「僵尸 job」会按心跳超时自动作废，
  不会永久占着位置让之后所有升级都撞 `busy`

主进程重启会让正在跑的 job 中断，界面会把这种情况显示为失败而不是永远转圈。
这一节把插件实际用到的能力写清楚，方便审核和排障时对照，而不是让人去读源码猜。

| 能力 | 范围 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 文件 | **仅 profile 目录** | 读写 `package.json`、写 `package.json.upgrader-journal.json`、读写并短暂持有 `package.json.lock`。不遍历文件系统，不碰 profile 以外的路径 |
| 网络（出站） | 配置的 npm 源、GitHub API | 只发 `GET`，见下 |
| 命令 | **无** | 不调用 `child_process`，不 spawn 任何进程；安装动作交给宿主的 `pluginManager` |
| 凭据 | **无** | 不读 token，不读 `.npmrc`，不做任何认证。私有源依赖 pnpm 自己的配置 |

安装源的选择（`registry` / `customRegistries`）由**宿主的设置服务**写进 profile 的
`cordis.patch.yml`，不是插件自己改文件——插件只调 `configForms` 的 `set()`。

宿主进程的环境变量只用了 `DSH_PROFILE_DIR` / `DSH_HOME` / `DSH_PROFILE` 三个来**定位 profile
目录**（桌面壳不导出它们时，退回「当前工作目录看起来像不像一个 profile」）。它们不是密钥，但
静态扫描器会把裸 `process.env` 记成一次「凭据」信号，这里说明清楚它的真实用途。

| 目标 | 用途 | 失败时 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{配置的 npm 源}/{包名}` | 拉 packument，列出已发布版本（5 分钟缓存，20 秒超时，最多 4 个并发） | 该行显示 `versionError` 和「重试」，其它行不受影响 |
| `https://registry.npmjs.org/{包名}` | 只当配置的不是官方源时，额外查一次上游，报告「镜像落后」 | 读不到就当作没有缺口 |
| `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags?per_page=100` | 取 tag 列表，判断某个版本号能不能链到 `releases/tag/v…`（30 分钟缓存，8 秒超时） | 退到 `releases` 列表页，绝不猜一个 404 的 tag |
| `{被测试的地址}/-/ping` 与根地址 | 「注册表」对话框里点「测试」时，**并发**探测这两条，谁先 2xx 用谁（整次探测 5 秒预算） | 报最具体的原因：状态码优先，其次超时，最后网络错误原文 |
| 本机 DSH Web 服务 | `/api/plugin-upgrader/*` 自己的五个路由 | — |

默认源是 pnpm 自己配置的那个（通常是 `.npmrc` 里的），也可以在「版本」页的「注册表」按钮里
换成官方源、大陆镜像或自己加的源。**没有任何遥测**，不向第三方发送使用数据。

运行时**没有自带依赖**。唯一的外部模块 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（Config schema 用，要求
`~3.18.5`）声明在 `peerDependencies` 里，由宿主提供——DSH 桌面端把它作为自身依赖发布，
`dsh-plugin-manager` 等第一方包也依赖它，所以 profile 里一定解析得到。构建和测试需要的那一份
放在 `devDependencies`。

`devDependencies` 其余各项（TypeScript、esbuild、`@types/*`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`）只在开发和
构建时使用，不会进入发布的 tarball 运行时。

- **一次只跑一批**：第二个提交拿 `409 busy`，界面接管正在跑的那一批，不报错。
- **job 心跳 2 秒**，15 分钟没进展判废，不会永久占位；主进程重启会中断正在跑的 job，
  界面显示为失败而不是永远转圈。
- **写入锁**：manager 自己的预算是 120 秒，超时会把锁的状态翻成人话（谁持有、要不要重启）。
  in-place 那条路自己也要这把锁，拿不到就在一秒内放弃并改走 remove + install，
  不会去改别人的 manifest。
- **升级失败**：in-place 替换会先把被摘掉的依赖记进 journal，失败就还原；进程被杀掉时，
  下次加载会把依赖补回去。还原时拿不到锁就保留 journal 等下次，不会先把记录清掉。
  失败了插件仍在、启用状态仍在。
- **还原了但没激活**：旧版本装回磁盘、宿主却没把它加载起来时，会明确说「文件在盘上，
  去『已安装』里重新启用」，而不是说「没装、去重装一遍」（重装只会得到 `already-installed`）。
  只有插件真的跑起来了，才算「已还原」。
- **registry 读不到 / GitHub 限流 / 离线**：都降级成「这一项读不到 + 原因 + 重试入口」，
  不会伪装成「没有新版本」「没有历史版本」。

要求 Node.js `>=20`，DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0`（`package.json` 的 `engines`）。
`dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` 只记录**真的跑过**的版本：

| DSH 版本 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| `0.2.1-rc.5` | compatible |

`0.2.1-rc.4` 和 `0.2.2-alpha.2` 虽然落在 `engines` 范围内，但没有逐一实测过，所以**不写进去**
（未声明的版本按 `unknown` 处理）。这是**来源侧的兼容声明**，不代替逐项的操作验收；
`dshOperations`（install / start / uninstall / rollback）同理，没有逐版本的实测记录就留空，
不写 `passed`。

readme.section: 每个版本对不对得上现在的 DSH
readme.text:
DSH 在装插件时会检查插件声明的 DSH 要求，不满足就**拒绝安装**。这个检查发生在版本已经被
摘掉之后（老路径是先卸再装），所以「点了切换，结果插件没了」是真实发生过的事。因此页面自己
先算一遍，规则和宿主完全一致：

- 插件声明了 `engines.dsh` 时，**只看它**，`peerDependencies` 被忽略；
- 否则，`peerDependencies` 里每一个 `@deepseek-ai/dsh`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 都要满足，
  `workspace:^` / `~` / `*` 视为「就是当前这个运行时」；
- 预发布版本参与比较（`includePrerelease`），与宿主的闸门相同。

两种方向都会标出来：DSH 升级之后想**降级**插件，历史里那些不再接受当前运行时的版本会
被标成「不支持当前 DSH」，切换按钮禁用；DSH 还停在旧版本时想**升级**，如果 `latest`
不接受当前运行时，它就不再算「可升级」，行上会写明它要的是哪个范围。

readme.section: 每个版本对不对得上现在的 DSH
readme.text:
运行时版本是从**宿主自己的入口**读的，不是从 profile 读的：profile 里的
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` 是指向 npx 缓存的链接，实测是 `0.1.2-rc.1`，而宿主真正报的是
`0.2.1-rc.5`。读不到时**什么都不标**——猜一个版本会把本来能装的版本说成不能装。

判定用的是 `src/host/version.ts` 里自己实现的区间匹配，已经在 49 个 range × 41 个版本共
2035 组上跟 `node-semver` 逐一对过（全部一致）。不引入 `semver` 依赖，是因为这条链路上
多一个运行时依赖就多一次供应链审阅，而这里需要的语义只有 `includePrerelease` 那一档。

```
dsh-plugin-upgrader/
├── AGENTS.md             **改代码前先读**：判据 + 守护测试，每条指向 docs/rules/ 的详证
├── docs/rules/           每条规则的详证页（事故现场、行号核对、原文存档；按需读，不自动加载）
├── src/                  源码（TypeScript）

浏览器端虽然拆成了多个 `.ts` 模块，但最终由 esbuild 打成一个 `lib/client.js`，
外面套上 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory(require) { … } })`。
运行时它只能 `require('react')` 这类由宿主提供的模块，不能 require 自己的其它文件，
所以「拆模块」只发生在源码层，产物仍然是单文件。

本项目用 pnpm 管理依赖（`package.json` 里钉了 `packageManager`，CI 也用 pnpm）：

```bash
pnpm install       # 只装依赖（不会构建，见下）
pnpm run dev       # 监听 src/，宿主端和浏览器端改完即编译（Ctrl+C 停止）
pnpm run build     # tsc 编译宿主端 + esbuild 打包 client → lib/
pnpm run typecheck # tsc 检查 src 和 test

`lib/` 是**提交进仓库**的，不是构建垃圾：DSH Store 审核固定 commit，不会为了补齐
运行时文件去执行 `prepare`。所以 `pnpm install` 不再触发构建（安装期脚本会被审核
直接否决），构建挂在 `prepack` 上；改完 `src/` 必须 `pnpm run build` 并把 `lib/`
一起提交，`pnpm run check` 会替你核对。详见 [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) 第 13 条
「`lib/` 是提交进仓库的，不是构建垃圾」。

**改任何代码前先读 [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)。** 那里列的是「已经实现、不能再退回」的行为，
每条都附了涉及的符号、守护它的测试名，以及一个 `docs/rules/` 详证页；`pnpm run check` 全绿
只说明没写坏，不说明没改坏（很多行为没有对应测试，比如「自己那一行不出现在批量升级里」
之外的边界情形）。

新增或修改测试后，问一句：**这个测试真的会红吗？** 把被测的字符串或分支临时改成哨兵值
再跑一次，确认它失败，然后改回来。不会失败的测试等于没写。

宿主端在 `src/index.ts`（`webServer` 前缀路由 `/api/plugin-upgrader`），
浏览器端在 `src/client/index.ts`（注册 `plugins.tab` 槽位）。

用户设置有两个：`registry`（当前在用的源，空 = 跟随 pnpm）和 `customRegistries`
（用户自己加的源），都在 `src/host/config.ts` 里声明成 `.volatile()`——这是宿主
设置服务愿意为它生成表单、并且写入能进到正在运行的插件里而不重启的唯一形状。
浏览器端通过 `configForms` 服务读写（`src/client/registry.ts`）；没有那个服务的
宿主照样能渲染这一页，只是源只能看不能改。两个自带源是常量，永远不写进
`customRegistries`，所以没有任何点击能改它们或删它们。

`pnpm run dev` 会并行跑两个监听器：`tsc --watch` 负责 `lib/index.js` 和
`lib/host/**`，esbuild 负责 `lib/client.js`，两者输出互不覆盖。注意 esbuild
打包时会直接剥掉类型而不做检查，所以改浏览器端时顺手跑一次 `pnpm run typecheck`。

改完代码后必须重新构建（profile 里的 `link:` 指向本目录，但加载的是 `lib/`，
不是 `src/`），并把重建后的 `lib/` 一起提交。`pnpm run dev` 已经替你重建了产物，
但**插件本身不会热更新**——要让宿主重新加载本插件，无需重启应用：先
`pluginManager.setBundleEnabled(name, false)` 再 `setBundleEnabled(name, true)`。

见 [RELEASING.md](./RELEASING.md)。首次手动发一次，之后打 `v*` tag 由 CI 通过 npm trusted publishing 自动发布：

```bash
pnpm publish --access public   # 仅首次
```

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-upgrader)
[](./LICENSE)
[](https://www.dsh.so/artifact/dsh-plugin-upgrader/)
[](https://www.dsh.so/artifact/dsh-plugin-upgrader/)
[](https://dsh.market/)
[](https://deepseekharnessplugins.com/plugins/zuwenyin/dsh-plugin-upgrader)

> One-click upgrades plus version history and rollback for the DeepSeek Harness
> **Plugins** page.

DSH's built-in Plugins page installs, removes and lists plugins, but two things are
missing: upgrading everything at once, and going back to an older version. This
plugin adds a **Versions** tab to that page and fills both gaps.

English · [中文](./README.md)

- **One-click upgrade** — bump every upgradable plugin to its newest version, with
  progress, per-plugin results and failure reasons.
- **Upgrades never unload the plugin** — a version replacement happens in place
  (see below), so the plugin is not torn down and reinstalled. When the profile's
  writer lock cannot be taken, or the in-place step is refused, it falls back to
  uninstall-then-install and says which reason it was.
- **Progress you can actually see** — the raw pnpm output (registry retries, lockfile
  verification), a live elapsed clock per step, an indeterminate bar while a step
  runs, and a cancel button that works.
- **Multi-select upgrade** — tick any subset of plugins and upgrade only those.
- **Version history / rollback** — expand any plugin to see every published version
  (with publish date and engine requirement) and switch to it in one click. Every
  version is first checked against the **DSH you are actually running**: releases
  this runtime cannot install are marked and their switch button is disabled (the
  host's gate refuses them only after the bundle has been unloaded).
- **GitHub links** — the `GH` button opens the plugin's repository; clicking a

> **Changing this repo? Read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first.** It lists the behaviour
> that already works and must keep working, with the code location and the test that
> guards each one. Two of those features (the `GH` links and the in-place upgrade)
> have already been lost once by accident.

A **Versions** tab appears next to *Installed* and the market tab on the Plugins
page (that tab is **Market** with `dshmarket` installed, and **Discover** in DSH's
own market page):

- Header counts: needing attention / upgradable / installed / version count
  (the first is a button: it narrows the list to the broken rows and stacks with the
  search box)
- The header **Registry** control opens the source dialog:
  - built-in sources (official registry, mainland mirror): switch to and test, never edit
    or delete
  - sources from `pluginManager`: use one directly, or keep it in your own list
  - sources you added: edit and delete; deleting the one in use falls back to
    *Follow pnpm's config*
  - **Test** on a row asks `/-/ping` and the registry root at the same time and keeps
    whichever answers first, with a 5 s budget for the whole probe (a sequential probe
    reported mainland mirrors as unreachable — their `/-/ping` can take 15 s while the
    root answers in 0.3 s), and shows the verdict under that row
  - the footer's *Follow pnpm's config* keeps pnpm's own registry (usually `.npmrc`)
- **Upgrade all** handles every upgradable plugin; the selection bar below handles
  **Upgrade selected**
- **Check for updates** bypasses the 5-minute registry cache
- The search box filters by package name
- The footer names the DSH version this page read, and whic

Search `dsh-plugin-upgrader` on the Plugins page's market tab (**Discover** in DSH
itself, **Market** with `dshmarket` installed) and hit install.
On the desktop app use its own plugin manager — the CLI cannot change the profile
an app has open.

With the `dsh` CLI (swap `web` for your profile name):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-upgrader
```

From source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zuwenyin/dsh-plugin-upgrader.git
cd dsh-plugin-upgrader
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD"
```

Open the Plugins page and the **Versions** tab is there. No build step, no restart.

A browser tab cannot read the profile's dependency list and cannot reliably reach
npm (CORS, private registries, tokens), so every package operation happens on the
host half:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/plugin-upgrader/overview` | installed plugins plus their published versions (registry packument, 5-minute cache, 20-second timeout, at most 4 concurrent) |
| `POST /api/plugin-upgrader/job` | queue a batch of upgrade / switch steps, return a job id immediately |
| `GET /api/plugin-upgrader/job?id=…` | poll progress, current phase, elapsed time, per-plugin results and the live log |
| `POST /api/plugin-upgrader/cancel` | abort the step in flight, whichever install is running |
| `GET /api/plugin-upgrader/host` | this process's pid and how it was started, for the "restart DSH" dialog |

Every route is loopback-only: a batch installs packages, so a paired remote device
or a cross-site page must never reach it.

readme.section: Why an upgrade does not unload the plugin
readme.text:
`pluginManager.installBundle` refuses a spec that names an already-installed
dependency (`already-installed`), so pnpm never runs. The order is therefore:

readme.section: Why an upgrade does not unload the plugin
readme.text:
1. **Install directly first.**
2. When that is refused, drop the dependency entry from the profile `package.json`
   (journal first) and install again — pnpm writes the new version back, the plugin is
   **not unloaded**, the loader keeps its instance, and no enabled state has to be
   restored.
3. Only when step 2 declines (unreadable manifest, no writer lock, failed install,
   refusal) does the old remove + install path run, and the log names which one it was.
   The previous version is reported back so the UI can warn about a downgrade.

readme.section: Why an upgrade does not unload the plugin
readme.text:
Step 2 edits `package.json` under **the harness's own writer lock** (`package.json.lock`),
the same one `plugin-manager` takes. If the lock cannot be taken it gives up within a
second and writes **not one byte**, then takes the always-correct fallback path — far
better than slipping an edit into somebody else's read-modify-write and losing the entry.

readme.section: Why an upgrade does not unload the plugin
readme.text:
> The code shipped in 1.2.0, but on the desktop app it **never actually ran** between
> 1.2.0 and 1.4.0: `profileDirFrom()` only knew `DSH_PROFILE_DIR` / `DSH_HOME` +
> `DSH_PROFILE`, and the desktop shell exports none of them (it starts the host with
> the profile directory as its working directory), so step 2 bailed on its first line
> and every upgrade quietly took the remove + install path. 1.4.1 added the working
> directory fallback. See item 2 of [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md), "replacing a version does
> **not** uninstall first".

Step 2 edits the profile `package.json` inside the window where the dependency entry is
gone and the new version is not written yet. A process killed in that window leaves the
plugin out of the manifest — uninstallable in effect. So a journal
(`package.json.upgrader-journal.json`) is written before the drop: the next plugin load
reads it, restores the entry when the manifest really lacks it, merely clears the record
when the install landed, and ignores a record that no longer describes the manifest.
A failed repair only logs; it never stops the tab from loading.

The record is only cleared once the entry is **confirmed back on disk under the lock**.
A restore that cannot take the lock fails and leaves the record for the next load:
clearing it after failing to write is exactly how a profile stops being repairable.

Removing a plugin drops its enabled / disabled state, so any step that really removes
one re-applies `setBundleEnabled` with the state it had before the upgrade. A disabled
plugin stays disabled after being upgraded.

readme.section: Why an upgrade sometimes takes minutes
readme.text:
Not this plugin: pnpm. Before installing, pnpm 11 re-checks every lockfile entry
against the registry (`Verifying lockfile against supply-chain policies`), and a
mirror such as `registry.npmmirror.com` answers `ETIMEDOUT` for plenty of packages,
which starts a 10-second → 1-minute retry ladder. The fallback path that really removes
and reinstalls costs two pnpm runs.

readme.section: Why an upgrade sometimes takes minutes
readme.text:
The old build showed nothing during that time and moved the bar once per completed
step, so it read as a hang. The host now subscribes to
`plugin-manager/install-log` and `plugin-manager/install-state` and streams pnpm's
own output, the phase and the retry count into the job log, while the panel shows an
elapsed clock and an indeterminate bar — a slow install looks like a retrying one
instead of a frozen 0%.

readme.section: Why an upgrade sometimes takes minutes
readme.text:
There are four phases: `verifying` (checking the lockfile) → `installing` →
`applying` / `cancelling`. The lockfile line can sit unchanged for minutes and reads
exactly like a hang, which is why it gets a phase name of its own.

The phase is read from *pnpm's own words*. The host announces `installing` before pnpm
even starts, so pnpm's later verification line still has to be able to name the phase
as `verifying` — until it gives the verdict (`✓ Lockfile passes supply-chain policies`).

readme.section: Why an upgrade sometimes takes minutes
readme.text:
"Is it still working?" is asked of the *host*, not of pnpm. pnpm stays quiet for a
minute during a registry retry, which is normal; judging a stall by "the log did not
change" reported healthy upgrades as stuck. The host re-stamps a heartbeat every two
seconds and the panel judges liveness by that, so only a host that really stopped
reporting is told so.

Two related bugs fixed with it:

readme.section: Why an upgrade sometimes takes minutes
readme.text:
- The heartbeat is a timer (2 s), no longer a write per completed step. A single step
  lasting over 15 minutes used to be declared abandoned, cancelling a healthy job and
  letting a second batch start on the same profile.
- The reinstall on the fallback path passed `requestId: undefined`, making that
  stretch uncancellable. Every install now has its own id, so cancel works throughout.

readme.section: A writer-lock timeout in plain words
readme.text:
The harness serializes writers of the profile `package.json` through a sibling
`package.json.lock`. The manager's own budget is 120 seconds, while `atomic-write`
defaults to 2 seconds for a caller that states none, so this shows up:

```
atomic-write: timed out waiting for the writer lock at …/package.json.lock
```

readme.section: A writer-lock timeout in plain words
readme.text:
That sentence names a file and a pid and nothing a reader can act on. The failure now
reads the lock first and says either "another operation is rewriting it, retry once it
finishes" or "the lock was never released, restarting DSH clears it", keeping the
original in brackets so it stays searchable.

readme.section: Its own row cannot upgrade itself
readme.text:
The first thing the batch path does is uninstall, and that would unload the very code
running it. So *Upgrade all* never includes this plugin, and its own row goes through
the Plugins page's own installer instead; a page that offers no install entry says so
rather than showing a button that cannot work.

The host runs one job at a time. A second submission gets `409 busy` with the id of
the job that is running, and the UI **adopts** that batch instead of showing an
error:

- opening a second Plugins tab, or clicking *Upgrade all* while a batch runs, shows
  the running batch
- `overview` carries an `active` field, so a freshly mounted tab reconnects to work
  in progress
- a job re-stamps a heartbeat every 2 seconds; a job left behind by a host restart is
  declared abandoned once the heartbeat goes stale, so it cannot block every later
  upgrade with a permanent `busy`

A restart interrupts the job in flight; the UI reports that as a failure rather than
spinning forever.

This section states the capabilities the plugin actually uses, so a review or a bug
report does not have to read the source to find out.

| Capability | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Files | **the profile directory only** | Reads and writes `package.json`, writes `package.json.upgrader-journal.json`, reads and briefly takes `package.json.lock`. No filesystem walking, nothing outside the profile |
| Network (outbound) | the configured npm registry, the GitHub API | `GET` only, see below |
| Commands | **none** | No `child_process`, no spawned processes; installs go through the host's `pluginManager` |
| Credentials | **none** | No tokens, no `.npmrc` reads, no authentication. Private registries rely on pnpm's own configuration |

The registry choice (`registry` / `customRegistries`) is written into the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml` by the **host's settings service**, not by the plugin editing files:
the plugin only calls `configForms.set()`.

Three environment variables are read, all to *locate the profile directory*:
`DSH_PROFILE_DIR`, `DSH_HOME` and `DSH_PROFILE`. When the desktop shell exports none of
them, a working directory that parses as a profile is used instead. They are not
secrets, but a bare `process.env` counts as one "credentials" signal in a static scan,
so the real purpose is spelled out here.

| Target | Purpose | On failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{configured npm registry}/{package}` | packument fetch, to list published versions (5 minute cache, 20 second timeout, at most 4 concurrent) | that row shows `versionError` and a retry entry; other rows are unaffected |
| `https://registry.npmjs.org/{package}` | only when the configured registry is not the official one: an extra upstream check that reports a lagging mirror | an unreadable upstream means "no gap", never "everything is missing" |
| `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags?per_page=100` | tag list, to decide whether a version can link to `releases/tag/v…` (30 minute cache, 8 second timeout) | falls back to the `releases` list; never guesses a tag that 404s |
| `{the address being tested}/-/ping` and its root | *Test* in the Registry dialog probes both **concurrently**, first 2xx wins (5 s budget for the whole probe) | reports the most specific reason: status code first, then timeout, then the raw network error |
| the local DSH web server | the plugin's own five `/api/plugin-upgrader/*` routes | — |

The default registry is whatever pnpm is configured with (usually `.npmrc`); the
**Registry** button on the Versions tab switches to the official registry, mainland
mirror, or a source you add yourself. **No telemetry** of any kind is sent.

There are **no bundled runtime dependencies**. The single external module,
`@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (used for the Config schema, `~3.18.5`), is declared in
`peerDependencies` and supplied by the host: DSH desktop ships it as its own dependency
and first-party packages such as `dsh-plugin-manager` depend on it too, so it always
resolves inside a profile. The copy needed for building and testing lives in
`devDependencies`.

The remaining `devDependencies` (TypeScript, esbuild, `@types/*`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`)
are development-time only and are not part of the published tarball's runtime.

- **One batch at a time**: a second submission gets `409 busy`; the UI adopts the batch
  that is running instead of reporting an error.
- **A job heartbeats every 2 seconds** and is declared abandoned after 15 minutes of
  no progress, so it cannot occupy the slot forever. A host restart interrupts the job
  in flight and the UI reports that as a failure.
- **Writer lock**: the manager's own budget is 120 seconds; a timeout is translated
  into who holds the lock and whether a restart clears it. The in-place path needs that
  same lock, gives up within a second, and falls back to remove + install rather than
  editing somebody else's manifest.
- **A failed upgrade**: the in-place path journals the dropped dependency before
  removing it and restores it on failure; a killed process is repaired on the next
  load. A restore that cannot take the lock keeps the record instead of clearing it,
  so the next load repairs it. The plugin stays installed and keeps its enabled state.
- **A rollback that lands but cannot activate** is reported as exactly that: the old
  version is back on disk, the host did not load it, and the panel tells you to
  re-enable it from the Installed tab instead

Node.js `>=20` and DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0` (the `engines` field).
`dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` records **only the releases actually exercised**:

| DSH release | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `0.2.1-rc.5` | compatible |

`0.2.1-rc.4` and `0.2.2-alpha.2` fall inside the `engines` range but were not each
exercised, so they are **not** listed (an undeclared release reads as `unknown`). These
are **source-side compatibility declarations**, not a substitute for per-operation
acceptance. `dshOperations` (install / start / uninstall / rollback) follows the same
rule: left out rather than filled with `passed` before there is a per-release run behind
it.

readme.section: Whether each version matches the DSH you run
readme.text:
DSH checks a plugin's declared DSH requirement at install time and **refuses** the install
when it does not hold. That check happens after the version has been taken out on the
older replacement path, which is how "I clicked switch and the plugin disappeared" really
happened. The page therefore reaches the verdict first, under exactly the host's rules:

readme.section: Whether each version matches the DSH you run
Whether each version matches the DSH you run
readme.text:
Both directions are covered: after DSH moves forward, releases in the history that no
longer admit this runtime are marked "not for this DSH" and their switch button is
disabled; while DSH stays behind, a `latest` that this runtime cannot install stops
counting as an upgrade, and the row says which range it wants instead.

readme.section: Whether each version matches the DSH you run
readme.text:
The runtime version is read from **the host's own entry point**, not from the profile: a
profile's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` is a link into an npx cache and measured
`0.1.2-rc.1` against a runtime that reports `0.2.1-rc.5`. When it cannot be read, nothing
is marked — a guessed version would call installable releases uninstallable.

readme.section: Whether each version matches the DSH you run
readme.text:
The matcher is implemented in `src/host/version.ts` and was checked against `node-semver`
over 49 ranges × 41 versions (2035 pairs, all agreeing). The `semver` package is not
pulled in because one more runtime dependency is one more supply-chain review, and the
only semantics needed here are the `includePrerelease` ones.

```
dsh-plugin-upgrader/
├── AGENTS.md             **read before changing code**: the rules plus their guard tests
├── docs/rules/           one detail page per rule (the incidents, line audits, archived text;
│                         read on demand — never auto-loaded)

The browser half is split into `.ts` modules, but esbuild bundles it back into a
single `lib/client.js` wrapped in `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory(require) { … } })`.
At runtime it can only `require` modules the host provides (`react`), not its own
siblings, so the split happens in the sources only.

Dependencies are managed with pnpm (`packageManager` is pinned in `package.json`,
and CI uses pnpm too):

```bash
pnpm install       # dependencies only — no build (see below)
pnpm run dev       # watch src/, rebuild the host and the client on save
pnpm run build     # tsc for the host + esbuild for the client → lib/
pnpm run typecheck # tsc over src and test

`lib/` is **committed**, not build litter: the DSH Store reviews a fixed commit and
will not run `prepare` to fill in missing runtime files. So `pnpm install` no longer
builds (install-time scripts are an automatic rejection in that review) and the build
hangs off `prepack`; after editing `src/` you must `pnpm run build` and commit `lib/`
with it, which `pnpm run check` verifies. See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) §13, "`lib/` is
committed, not build litter".

The host half lives in `src/index.ts` (a `webServer` prefix route at
`/api/plugin-upgrader`), the browser half in `src/client/index.ts` (registering the
`plugins.tab` slot).

The user settings are `registry` (the source in use, empty for "follow pnpm") and
`customRegistries` (the sources the user added), both declared in `src/host/config.ts`.
Both are marked `.volatile()`, which is what makes the host's settings service expose a
form for them and what lets a write reach the running plugin without a DSH restart. The
browser reads and writes them through the `configForms` client service
(`src/client/registry.ts`); a host without that service still renders the tab, with the
source shown but not editable. The two built-in sources are constants, never entries in
`customRegistries` — that is why no click can edit or delete them.

`pnpm run dev` runs two watchers side by side: `tsc --watch` owns `lib/index.js`
and `lib/host/**`, esbuild owns `lib/client.js`, so neither overwrites the other.
esbuild only strips types, it does not check them — run `pnpm run typecheck` after
editing the browser half.

Either way the profile's `link:` points at this directory but loads `lib/`, not
`src/`, so the build has to run and the rebuilt `lib/` has to be committed with it.
`pnpm run dev` keeps the output current, but the plugin itself does **not**
hot-reload — reload it without restarting the app by calling
`pluginManager.setBundleEnabled(name, false)` and then
`setBundleEnabled(name, true)`.
